donts: Don't hide the QR code behind a tap or a popover.
Don't use mono for anything that is not an ID, code, or timestamp.
Don't add gradients, glass, or shadows to this system.
Don't add a second accent colour — amber is only for waiting, red only for stop.
Don't use an eyebrow/kicker label above a heading.
dos: Do keep the QR code the largest, highest-contrast element on the screen.
Do pair every colour-coded state with a word ("Connected", "Listening…").
Do use 48px minimum touch targets for every action.
Do keep send progress honest: a "Sending…" button state, then a history entry — never a faked progress bar (PeerJS reports no byte progress).
keyCharacteristics: Paper ground, ink panels, one signal teal — colour does real jobs (live, listening, done), never decoration.
Flat panels with thin ink borders; no gradients, no glass, no shadows as decoration.
Mono type only for IDs, codes, and timestamps — never as a costume.
Big touch targets (48px minimum), status always paired with a word, never colour alone.
narrative.overview: The screen is a signal, not a form. One phone beams a file straight to the phone next to it — no server, no upload — and the interface shows that beam: a large QR code as the address, a vertical line joining three steps that fills in as each one completes, and connection state said in plain words with a signal meter beside it. The world is paper and ink with a single signal teal; the QR hero is the one dark moment on the page, so the brightest thing on screen is always the code someone needs to scan.

rules.body: Teal means the beam is live. Nothing else on the screen is teal, and nothing live is any other colour except amber while it waits.
rules.name: The One Signal Rule

rules.body: If it is not an ID, a code, or a timestamp, it is not set in mono.
rules.name: The Mono Is Data Rule

rules.body: No shadows. A panel that needs emphasis gets a darker ground or a thicker border, not a blur.
rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
